title: Root Cause Hypothesis Matrix and Probe Realignment
author: Priya Nair
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines a structured hypothesis matrix for root-cause analysis of quality regressions and prescribes a probe realignment workflow to remediate regressions with minimal user impact. It is intended for SREs, evaluators, model owners, and the regression-triage oncall rotation.

Scope
-----
- Applies to production or shadow regressions where an SQC (service-level quality contract) metric crosses alert thresholds (see "When to use").
- Covers classification of candidate causes, prioritized probe (test) selection, telemetry enrichment, and rollback/mitigation actions.
- Does NOT replace incident postmortems; it is a tactical investigation and containment template.

When to use
-----------
Trigger conditions (any):
- Fidelity delta >= 7% on a critical slice in the last 24h.
- Regression impact index > 0.15 for a customer-facing route.
- Sudden increase in semantic-failure sentinel alerts (x10 baseline).

Ownership and roles
-------------------
- Incident lead: regression-triage oncall (primary owner for the first 4 hours).
- Model owner: responsible for model-level hypothesis validation and rollout decisions.
- Evaluator engineer: runs targeted probes and annotator reconciliation.
- Telemetry engineer: enriches traces and ensures probe instrumentation.
- Customer-facing PM/CS: informed if a customer SLA or QBR-affecting route is impacted.

Hypothesis matrix (quick reference)
-----------------------------------
Columns: hypothesis id, short description, likely signal sources, priority (H/M/L), canonical probes to run, quick mitigations

| HYP ID | Hypothesis | Signals to check | Priority | Probes | Quick mitigations |
|--------|-----------|------------------|---------:|-------|------------------|
| H1 | Prompt / prompt-template drift (priming layer change) | Prompt hash drift, increased parsing errors, high edit-distance from baseline | H | exact-match probe, fewshot-variance probe | Reapply canonical prompt, enable prompt-safelist fallback |
| H2 | KV-cache warmup or eviction regression (context loss) | Spike in cold-start latency, increased token count, cache-miss-rate > 8% | H | warmup-sequence replay, context-fidelity probe | Shorten TTL, enable KV-cache-prefill for hot tenants |
| H3 | Quantization-induced coherence failure | Phase-aligned increase in hallucination or inconsistent tokens after quant rollout | H | quant-contrast probe, low-temp stochastic replay | Roll back quant profile to last stable artifact |
| H4 | Serving runtime scheduling or batching change | Tail latency spikes, batching-size variance, throughput mismatch | M | microburst replay, latency-tail probe | Pin previous autoscaler, reduce batch size for affected routes |
| H5 | Tokenizer/tokenization change or model tokenizer mismatch | Tokenization mismatch errors, token length distribution shift | M | tokenization-diff probe, canonical-tokenization test | Revert tokenizer version, apply token-normalizer preprocessor |
| H6 | Upstream pre-processor or data transform change | Input normalization variance, increased input failures | M | transform-invariant probe | Revert transformation, enable legacy transform path |
| H7 | Annotation/labeling drift in evaluation set | Increased annotator disagreement, label-coverage gaps | L | annotation-consistency audit | Pause auto-promotions, request annotator relabeling |
Note: priorities reflect operational impact; H are investigated first.

Probe realignment workflow (step-by-step)
-----------------------------------------
1) Triage (first 30 minutes)
   1.1 Acknowledge pager and assign incident lead.
   1.2 Capture the baseline: which model-version(s), routes, and slices are affected.
   1.3 Record the initial telemetry snapshot (last 72h): drift_index, fidelity_delta, latency_p95, cache_miss_rate.

2) Hypothesis selection (30-90 minutes)
   2.1 Use the Hypothesis Matrix to pick top 2–3 candidate causes.
   2.2 For each candidate, list 1 canonical probe and 1 lightweight smoke check.

3) Probe execution and telemetry enrichment (90–240 minutes)
   3.1 Run canonical probes in shadow; keep live traffic untouched unless customer risk requires mitigation.
   3.2 Enrich telemetry streams: add the following tags to affected traces: model_version, probe_id, probe_seed_id, tenant_id (anonymized).
   3.3 Collect per-token diagnostics for a minimum of 5k examples or 2 hours of traffic, whichever is smaller.

4) Analysis and decisioning (240–360 minutes)
   4.1 If a single hypothesis explains >= 80% of the failing probes, escalate to the model owner for rollback or patch.
   4.2 If multiple hypotheses are plausible, schedule a micro-canary (see Canary guidance below) or enact short-term mitigations (fallback model, cached responses).

5) Mitigation and follow-up (post 6 hours)
   5.1 Deploy mitigation (rollback, config pin, traffic split) and monitor key SLOs for 2x the time-to-detection.
   5.2 Create an incident summary with the hypothesis matrix annotated with results and attach probe artifacts.

Canary guidance (micro-canary template)
--------------------------------------
- Size: 0.1% – 1% of production traffic depending on customer impact and model sensitivity.
- Duration: minimum 30 minutes, prefer 1–3 hours for behavioural checks.
- Metrics to watch: fidelity_delta, regression_impact_index, token_repetition_rate, latency_p95.
- Safety gates: automatic rollback if fidelity_delta > 5% or customer_error_rate doubles.

Probe design patterns and examples
--------------------------------
- Canonical exact-match probe (YAML example):
  ---
  probe_id: probe.exact_match.v1
  dataset_source: seedstore://probe-seeds/exact-match-core
  selection: stratified_by_slice
  executor: shadow-replay
  postchecks:
    - exact-match-percent >= 98
    - response_length_median within 5 tokens of baseline

- Quant-contrast probe (cli example):
  # run quant-contrast against current quant artifact and baseline float artifact
  ./eval-tools quant-contrast --baseline s3://models/modelA/float/2025-11-05 --candidate s3://models/modelA/quant/q3 --slices long-context,faq,legal --output report.json

Telemetry and instrumentation checklist
--------------------------------------
- Ensure probes emit: probe_id, seed_id, slice_tag, model_version, artifact_id, runtime_kernel_tag.
- Per-token telemetry for 1 sample per 1000 requests by default, increased to 1 per 100 during active triage.
- Retention: probe traces kept for 90 days for triage artifacts; aggregated metrics retained according to analytics policy.
- Privacy: tenant identifiers must be hashed with company KMS salt before inclusion. No raw PII allowed.

Decision matrix for actions (quick lookup)
-----------------------------------------
- If probe confirms H1 or H5 (prompt/tokenizer): immediate rollback of recent prompt/tokenizer change OR enable safelist fallback.
- If probe confirms H2 or H4 (runtime/cache/scheduling): throttle affected route, pin autoscaler config, short-term route diversion to dedicated pool.
- If probe confirms H3 (quantization): rollback quant profile; if rollback impossible, increase temperature and enable coherence postprocessors for affected routes.
- If no hypothesis reaches 60% explanation after probes: open a deep-investigation incident and schedule a 24h follow-up with model and runtime owners.

Artifact and evidence capture (required fields)
----------------------------------------------
Every triage must attach a digital artifact bundle with these files:
- probe_manifest.json (list of probes executed and parameters)
- sample_responses.jsonl (anonymized seed_id, request, response, token_diagnostics) — max 10k rows
- telemetry_snapshot.csv (metrics used to trigger triage)
- decision_log.md (who signed off, rationale, mitigation steps)

Post-incident learning and probe realignment
-----------------------------------------
1) If root cause confirmed, update the Hypothesis Matrix weights for similar slices and add or retire canonical probes.
2) If a probe false-positive was costly (time/resource), mark probe for recalibration and add an acceptance test to the probe CI.
3) Quarterly: reconcile the probe seedset to ensure coverage of newly observed failure modes (responsibility: Evaluator team).

Appendix A — Example decision_log.md template
-----------------------------------------------
Incident: R-2026-042
Start: 2026-01-12T09:17Z
Lead: priya.nair@redwood.com
Hypotheses tested: H2, H3
Outcome: H3 confirmed (quant-coherence regression). Rolled back q3 profile to q2 at 2026-01-12T13:08Z.
Follow-up: Create a micro-eval gate for the quant pipeline; add quant-contrast probe to pre-promotion suite.

Appendix B — Common CLI shortcuts
----------------------------------
- Start a shadow probe run: evalctl probe run --manifest probe_manifest.yaml --mode shadow --timeout 2h
- Snapshot telemetry: telemetryctl snapshot --metrics drift_index,fidelity_delta,cache_miss_rate --since 72h --out telemetry_snapshot.csv
- Package artifact bundle: incidentctl package --probe-manifest probe_manifest.json --samples sample_responses.jsonl --out R-<id>-bundle.tar.gz

Notes and caveats
------------------
- This workflow assumes evaluators and runtime engineers can run shadow probes without impacting production. If your environment isolates shadow traffic differently, adjust the probe executor accordingly.
- Always prioritize customer-facing routes and regulated tenants in decisioning.

Related references
------------------
- See the Regression Impact Index spec for scoring details.
- See the Eval Harness orchestration guide for probe scheduling SLA.

Questions or improvements
------------------------
Open a PR against this page or ping #regression-triage in Slack. For changes affecting probe CI, include Evaluator team in reviewers (e.g., evelyn.chen@redwood.com).
